title: Proposed international clinical diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular edema disease severity scales
passage: Paraphrased summary: the international clinical scale has five levels - no apparent retinopathy, mild non-proliferative DR (microaneurysms only), moderate non-proliferative DR (more than microaneurysms but less than severe), severe non-proliferative DR, and proliferative DR (neovascularisation and/or vitreous or preretinal haemorrhage).

title: Standards of Care in Diabetes - Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care
publisher: American Diabetes Association (Diabetes Care, annual supplement)
version: current annual edition - confirm year at use
passage: Paraphrased summary: people with any level of macular edema, moderate or worse non-proliferative DR, or any proliferative DR should be referred to an ophthalmologist experienced in DR management; retinal photography with remote reading can serve as a screening tool but is not a substitute for a comprehensive eye examination.

title: Standards of Care in Diabetes - Foot Care
publisher: American Diabetes Association (Diabetes Care, annual supplement)
version: current annual edition - confirm year at use
passage: Paraphrased summary: a comprehensive foot evaluation at least annually is recommended for people with diabetes to identify risk factors for ulcers and amputation, with more frequent inspection for those with high-risk features.

title: KDIGO 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in Chronic Kidney Disease
publisher: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (Kidney International)
passage: Paraphrased summary: kidney involvement in diabetes is assessed with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and estimated GFR, generally at least annually; staging and treatment decisions rest on those measurements, not on imaging surrogates.

title: Retinal microvascular abnormalities and their relationship with hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and mortality
publisher: Survey of Ophthalmology (Wong TY et al.)
passage: Paraphrased summary: population studies report associations between retinal microvascular signs (e.g. arteriolar narrowing, arteriovenous nicking, retinopathy) and hypertension and cardiovascular outcomes; these are population associations and do not establish an individual diagnosis.

title: A portable retinal imaging dataset of people with diabetes from Brazil (mBRSET)
passage: Paraphrased summary: mBRSET contains 5,164 images from 1,291 people with diabetes captured with a handheld smartphone-based fundus camera after pharmacological dilation, with image-quality, ICDR grading and self-reported clinical metadata. Model performance on this dataset does not transfer automatically to other cameras or populations.

title: Diabetic Retinopathy Preferred Practice Pattern
passage: Paraphrased summary: the recommended follow-up interval and management depend on the retinopathy level and presence of centre-involving macular edema, as determined by examination; the ophthalmologist communicates findings back to the primary care physician managing the patient's diabetes.
